items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls or sessions; it only sees the text in the current call, so without saved notes it cannot know. Options b, c and d each assume the model remembers on its own.
Call 1 sends 2,000. Call 2 sends 2,000 + 100 + 500 = 2,600. Total 4,600. An answer of 2,600 counts only the last call; an answer of 2,000 or 2,100 ignores that the history is sent again.
Retrieval keeps long material outside the window and fetches only the best chunks per question. Pasting everything is resent every call and hurts attention; the model cannot memorise during a chat.

items.answer: Training status goes in notes because it changes slowly and must survive between visits; the printer's availability is looked up live because the calendar changes constantly.
accepted: training status in notes, printer availability from the calendar tool
notes for training status, live lookup for printer availability
training status is saved, printer calendar is checked live because it changes
items.rationale: Slow-changing per-student facts go in notes; fast-changing facts are fetched from the tool each time or they go stale. Swapping the two is the typical error.

Clearing old tool results (leaving a pointer to search again) is the lightest form of compaction. Deleting instructions or recent turns breaks the task, and discarding the whole chat loses everything.
